title: Pretending
goal: Say that someone is pretending, and that you pretended, with -mIş gibi yapmak.

intro.text: *Gibi yapmak* means **to pretend**. The pretended state takes `-mIş` or `-(I)yormuş`, and the person and tense go on *yapmak*: *Uyuyormuş gibi yaptım* (I pretended to be asleep). Colloquially: *numara yapmak*.

vocab.en: act, trick; number (numara yapmak: to fake it, to put on an act)
role, part (rol yapmak: to act a part, to put on an act)
to imitate, to do an impression of

exercises.question: *Uyuyormuş gibi yaptı.* What did she do?
exercises.explain: `-mIş gibi yapmak` is **to pretend**: *uyuyormuş gibi yaptı*.

exercises.text: Ders ___ gibi yapıyor, ama aslında telefonla oynuyor.
exercises.en: He's pretending to study, but he's actually playing on his phone.

reject.why: Before *gibi yapmak*, the pretended action takes `-mIş` too: *çalışıyormuş gibi*.
Turkish **pretend** never takes the infinitive: *çalışıyormuş gibi yapıyor*.

exercises.explain: *çalış-ıyor-muş gibi yapıyor*: he's pretending to be studying.

reject.why: That says he **didn't pretend to understand**. Negate the pretended state: *anlamamış gibi yaptı*.

exercises.explain: **Pretend not to**: the negative goes on the state, *anla-ma-mış gibi*, and *yapmak* stays positive.

accept: He is pretending to be sick.
He is pretending to be ill.

exercises.explain: *Uyu-* ends in a vowel, so the present continuous is just *-yor*; then *-muş*, rounded after o.

exercises.en: Don't pretend to listen to me, listen!

exercises.question: Which is the everyday way to say **he's faking it**?
exercises.explain: *Numara yapmak* is colloquial for **to fake it, to put on an act**.

exercises.prompt: Çocuklar uyuyormuş gibi yaptılar ama gülüyorlardı.
exercises.text: The children pretended to be asleep, but they were laughing.

exercises.prompt: Çok inandırıcı rol yaptı; herkesi kandırdı.
accept: She put on a very convincing act; she fooled everyone.
She put on a very convincing act; she tricked everyone.
She [acted|pretended|played her part] very convincingly; she [fooled|tricked] everyone.
She [put on a very convincing act|acted very convincingly|pretended very convincingly|played her part very convincingly] and [fooled|tricked] everyone.
He [put on a very convincing act|acted very convincingly|pretended very convincingly|played his part very convincingly]; he [fooled|tricked] everyone.
He [put on a very convincing act|acted very convincingly|pretended very convincingly|played his part very convincingly] and [fooled|tricked] everyone.

exercises.task: Write three short sentences about times when you, or someone you know, pretended something: to be asleep, to be ill, to be busy, or not to have heard. Use `-mIş gibi yapmak` or `-(I)yormuş gibi yapmak`.
models: Çocukken sabahları bazen hasta numarası yapardım. Annem odama gelince uyuyormuş gibi yapardım. Kardeşim de beni hiç duymamış gibi yapardı.
Dün toplantıda Murat dinliyormuş gibi yaptı, ama aslında mesajlarına bakıyordu. Ben de anlamış gibi yaptım, çünkü sormaktan utandım. Sonra ikimiz de güldük.
checklist: The pretended state takes `-mIş` or `-(I)yormuş`: *uyuyormuş gibi*
**Pretend not to** negates the state: *duymamış gibi*

exercises.en: Don't pretend you don't know anything.
He was pretending to snore, but he wasn't asleep.
exercises.explain: The tense goes on *yapmak*: *horluyormuş gibi yapıyordu*, **he was pretending to snore**.
